This chapter reports, for every fitted model of the current analysis set, the checks of the assumptions on which its tests rest. The models themselves are not changed by these checks.

Conditional residuals (observation minus fitted value including the random effects), standardised by the residual SD: QQ plot and histogram against the normal distribution; skewness and excess kurtosis (0 for a normal distribution); share of standardised residuals beyond ±3 (.0027 for a normal distribution); Shapiro-Wilk test on at most 5,000 residuals; residuals and √|residual| against the fitted values, with the Spearman correlation of |residual| and fitted value; ratio of the largest to the smallest residual SD of the three instruction conditions. Participant random effects: QQ plots and the smallest Shapiro-Wilk p over the random-effect terms. Fit: singular fit and convergence messages. Collinearity: largest variance inflation factor of the main-effect terms (interaction terms are left out because their variance inflation factors are inflated by construction).
Raw residuals of these models have no reference distribution. Simulation-based quantile residuals are used instead (

): the fitted model is simulated 250 times, and the residual of an observation is the randomised proportion of simulated values below it. Under a correct model they are uniform. Reported are the Kolmogorov-Smirnov test of uniformity, the dispersion ratio (variance of the observations around the simulated mean relative to the same quantity in the simulations; 1 if the dispersion is reproduced) with its simulation p-value, and the share of observations outside all simulated values.
QQ plot, residuals and √|standardised residual| against fitted values, Shapiro-Wilk test, Koenker’s studentised Breusch-Pagan test, and Cook’s distance per participant.

A model is flagged for inspection of its figure when |skewness| > 1, |excess kurtosis| > 3 or more than 1 % of standardised residuals lie beyond ±3 (residual shape); when |ρ(|residual|, fitted)| > .2, the residual SD ratio between conditions exceeds 1.5 or the Breusch-Pagan p < .01 (residual variance); when the quantile residuals deviate from uniformity (KS p < .01) or the dispersion test has p < .05; when a participant random effect deviates from normality (Shapiro-Wilk p < .01); when a variance inflation factor exceeds 5; when the largest Cook’s distance exceeds 0.5; and for singular fits and convergence messages. With several thousand observations, the Shapiro-Wilk and KS tests detect departures that are too small to matter, so that the decisive information is the size of the departure in the figures and in the skewness, kurtosis and dispersion values. The thresholds are conventions for screening and are not decisions about the models.
